name: Ivan Ruiz
home: the western blocks near Ferry Street Rooms
life: “I still remember meeting an heir who needed permission to disappoint a parent.” People around the market by Market Flats know Ivan by a small Friday habit. Ivan often waits until the delivery baskets are stacked before going in.
voice: I would give my right arm to inherit a place. Listening to the daughter made me reconsider what a gift with no exit costs.
appearance: Ivan has black hair twisted into a small knot, a long face and high cheekbones, and a favorite piece of clothing, a sand-colored linen shirt. It usually goes with a tiny red thread tied through the lowest buttonhole. When somebody else has the floor, Ivan looks down for a moment before saying something difficult.
personality: Ivan has a talent for getting adversaries to laugh at exactly the same thing. Ivan knows better than to expect the laugh to settle what they are arguing about.
agenda: To listen to the heir without comparing family fortunes.
family: Cynthia Barrett is Ivan’s second cousin. Ivan gets to change the plan. Cynthia offers the first invitation. They learned that a promise to visit is easier to keep when changing a time does not count as letting down the whole family. Asked about *The first language*, Cynthia says, “I wrote an alphabet on the inside of my lunch tin so I could practice without answering questions.”
connections: Keir Rios. A donor's dinner gets easier once two people can explain why it is possible to refuse a gift.

reactions.response: Ivan takes the daughter's preferred shop seriously before proposing another gift.
